records.section_heading: The Impact of Acanthaster planci Coral Kills on the
records.question: By how much did live coral cover at Cape Larsen decrease after Acanthaster planci coral kills?
records.ground_truth_answer: It decreased from 70% to less than 20% (visually estimated).
ground_truth_chunks: Cape Larsen was surveyed 3 times before A. planci reduced the live coral cover from 70% to less than 20% (visually estimated).

records.question: How many crown-of-thorns starfish were removed in less than one year after the outbreak at Tutuila?
records.ground_truth_answer: 486,933 crown-of-thorns starfish were removed in less than one year after the outbreak.
ground_truth_chunks: Despite the removal of 486,933 crown-of-thorns starfish in less than one year after the outbreak (Birkeland 1982)(Figure 2), most of the live coral habitat surrounding Tutuila was destroyed.
Figure 2. <u>Acanthaster planci</u>. Numbers removed from the ocean for bounty (open numbers) or observed in surveys (numbers in parentheses) at Tutuila, American Samoa. (from Birkeland, 1982)

records.question: In the transects the author ("I") censused, what method was used to estimate live coral cover and how many points/colonies were sampled along each transect?
records.ground_truth_answer: The point-quarter method recommended by Birkeland and Amesbury was used; twenty points (80 coral colonies) were sampled along each transect.
ground_truth_chunks: In the transects I censused, the live coral cover and the genus composition was estimated by the point-quarter method recommended by Birkeland and Amesbury (Attachment A). Twenty points (80 coral colonies) were sampled along each transect.
At Cape Larsen, along the 20 ft depth contour, I sampled at least 8 points (32 coral colonies) in each of two 30 m long replicates with the point-quarter method.

records.question: What was the percent live coral cover for the 20 ft depth contour at Cape Larsen in October 1986?
ground_truth_chunks: The percent live coral cover for the 20 ft depth contour at Cape Larsen increases from 7.58% in April 1982 to 22.34% in April 1985 to 24.70% in October 1986.

records.question: Which fish species showed a significant increase (P < 0.05) in number according to the t' test results reported in the Discussion?
ground_truth_chunks: Two labrids showed significant changes. Bodianus axillaris significantly (P < 0.05) reduced in number, and Halichoeres hortulanus significantly increased in number.
Naso lituratus, an algal grazing acanthurid (Amesbury and Myers 1982), increased in number significantly (P < 0.05).
